facts.statement: Barreirosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: This extinct genus was found in the Late Cretaceous of São Paulo State in southeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Barreirosuchus is an extinct genus of itasuchid notosuchian known from the Late Cretaceous of São Paulo State, southeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 2000 near Monte Alto County in the Serra do Jabuticabal escarpment of the Bauru Basin.
facts.quote: It was found in the year 2000 four kilometer from Monte Alto County, in the escarpment of the Serra do Jabuticabal within the Bauru Basin

facts.statement: The genus was first described by Fabiano Vidoi Iori and Karina Lucia Garcia in 2012.
facts.quote: Barreirosuchus was first named by Fabiano Vidoi Iori and Karina Lucia Garcia in 2012

facts.statement: The species name honors paleontologist Cledinei Aparecido Francisco for his technical support during the excavation.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the paleontologist Cledinei Aparecido Francisco from the Museu de Paleontologia de Monte de Alto, for technical support during the excavations of the holotype.

facts.statement: The only known specimen is a posterior skull portion containing six teeth and four vertebrae.
facts.quote: Barreirosuchus is known only from the holotype specimen MPMA-04-0012/00, an undeformed posterior portion of the skull with six teeth and a series of four vertebrae, two dorsal and two sacral.

facts.statement: A detailed redescription including internal anatomy via CT scans was published by Fachini and colleagues in 2025.
facts.quote: A more detailed redescription of the skull material was later published by Fachini and colleagues in 2025, not simply focusing on the external anatomy of the specimen but also detailing the internal anatomy, which were acquired via computed tomography.

facts.statement: The skull is robust, moderately tall, and wider than it is tall.
facts.quote: The skull of Barreirosuchus is described as robust and though moderately tall still wider than tall.

facts.statement: Although the snout is mostly missing, the head is inferred to have been roughly triangular.
facts.quote: While most of the snout is missing the head has been inferred to have been roughly triangular in shape.

facts.statement: The skull is interpreted as having a flattened, platyrostral snout.
facts.quote: It has been interpreted as having had a flattend (platyrostral) snout.

facts.statement: The skull surface features small circular pits and ridges, especially on the jugal and skull table.
facts.quote: The surface of the skull is ornamented by a pattern of small, circular pits, It has been interpreted as having had a flattend (platyrostral) snout. ridges and grooves, which are most prominent on the jugal and the skull table.

facts.statement: A prominent feature is a median boss, a raised dome before the eyes formed by multiple skull bones.
facts.quote: A prominent feature of Barreirosuchus is the presence of a median boss, a raised dome-like structure located before the eyes formed by the maxillae, prefrontals, lacrimal bones, nasal boness, jugals and the frontal bone.

facts.statement: The eye sockets are positioned dorsolaterally, higher on the skull than in related terrestrial forms.
facts.quote: The eyesockets of Barreirosuchus are located dorsolaterally, meaning they were positioned higher up on the skull than in terrestrial forms such as peirosaurids and baurusuchids.

facts.statement: The parietal bone gives the skull table an hourglass shape.
facts.quote: The parietal forms the space between the fenestrae and the medial posterior edge of the skull table, giving it an hourglass-shape.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, Barreirosuchus franciscoi.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Barreirosuchus franciscoi.

facts.statement: It closely resembles Caririsuchus camposi and Itasuchus jesuinoi, sharing several synapomorphies with them.
facts.quote: It most closely resembles Caririsuchus camposi from the Araripe Basin and Itasuchus jesuinoi also from the Bauru Basin, and shares with them several synapomorphies.

facts.statement: The fossil was found near a cave where the snout had already been eroded away.
facts.quote: The fossil was recovered near a cave with the upper surface of the skull exposed and the anterior parts of the snout already eroded away.

facts.statement: The shape of the postorbital bar in Barreirosuchus contributes to the depth of the skull by distancing the skull roof from the jugal bone.
facts.quote: Overall the shape of postorbital bar of Barreirosuchus contributes to the depth of the skull, distancing the skull roof from the jugal.

facts.statement: The preserved teeth of Barreirosuchus are described as blunt, rounded, and having an oval cross-section.
facts.quote: Those that were preserved are described as blunt and rounded with an oval cross-section.

facts.statement: The teeth of Barreirosuchus are low-crowned and taller than they are wide.
facts.quote: They are also noted to be low-crowned and following Fachini and colleagues taller than wide.

facts.statement: The teeth of Barreirosuchus are subtly labiolingually flattened, bear striations near the base, show signs of a keel on at least one tooth, but lack serrations.
facts.quote: Iori and Garcia furthermore describe them as being subtly labiolingually flattened and bearing striations along close to the base and at least one shows signs of a keel, but no serrations.

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus had a skull shape that closely resembles modern gharials and freshwater crocodiles.
facts.quote: The overall shape closely resembles modern gharials and freshwater crocodiles

facts.statement: The olfactory tract of Barreirosuchus featured grooves on either side that gave its dorsal surface a vaulted appearance.
facts.quote: The olfactory tract has also been noted for featuring a groove on either side, given the dorsal surface a vaulted appearance

facts.statement: In Barreirosuchus, the transition between the forebrain and midbrain forms a 170° angle, while the transition from midbrain to hindbrain forms an angle of around 120°.
facts.quote: The transition between fore- and midbrain sits at a 170° angle, while the transition from mid- to hindbrain exhibits an angle of around 120°

facts.statement: The skull of Barreirosuchus displays well-developed cranial pneumaticity due to an expanded system of paratympanic sinuses.
facts.quote: The skull of Barreirosuchus shows well developed cranial pneumaticity thanks to an expanded system of paratympanic sinuses

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Barreirosuchus consists of four vertebrae: the last two dorsal/lumbar and the first two sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Barreirosuchus includes four vertebrae, specifically the last two dorsal/lumbar vertebrae and the first two sacral vertebrae

facts.statement: The entire body of Barreirosuchus may have been around 4 meters long.
facts.quote: The entire body may have been around 4 m

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus is thought to have been semiaquatic, similar to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Barreirosuchus is thought to have been semiaquatic, much like modern crocodilians

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus had eyes angled upward and positioned high on the skull, allowing it to keep its eyes above the water surface in lakes or rivers.
facts.quote: Its eyes were angled upward and were positioned higher than most of the skull, allowing the animal to keep its eyes above the surface of the water if it were in a lake or river

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus belongs to the parent group Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Itasuchidae

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus is classified in the family Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Itasuchidae

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Barreirosuchus is Barreirosuchus franciscoi.
facts.quote: Type species: Barreirosuchus franciscoi

facts.statement: Barreirosuchus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
